common_name: Screamin' Yellow Baptisia (Vivid Golden-Yellow Compact False Indigo)

planting.note: Plant container plants in spring in well-drained, average soil in full sun, choosing a permanent site since Baptisia develops a deep taproot and resents transplanting once established; Screamin' Yellow is a compact Baptisia sphaerocarpa selection bearing exceptionally vivid, saturated golden-yellow flower spikes.

directions: Plant in well-drained, average soil in full sun, choosing a permanent site since Baptisia develops a deep taproot and does not transplant well once established. Screamin' Yellow is a compact selection of the naturally yellow-flowered Baptisia sphaerocarpa, bred for unusually vivid, saturated golden-yellow flower spikes on a tidier, more floriferous plant than typical seedling-grown yellow wild indigo, blooming heavily in late spring above attractive blue-green, clover-like foliage. Following bloom, dark seedpods provide fall and winter interest, and the plant serves as a larval host for several native butterfly species while its flowers draw bumblebees. It is extremely drought-tolerant and essentially maintenance-free once established, functioning almost like a small flowering shrub in the perennial border. Avoid dividing or transplanting mature plants; simply cut back in late winter if a tidier form is wanted.
